log.action: Stride toward the sound of the whip.
log.narration: Turn 1 | Day 1, 6:03 pmYou break into a run, boots pounding the ash-choked earth, chainmail chiming with each stride. The South Road bends around a stand of dead, blackened trees, and past them you see it: a merchant caravan, three wagons pulled up short, oxen screaming and thrashing in their traces. Men in studded leather swarm the wagons like wolves on a wounded elk, and one merchant already lies face-down in the dirt, a red ruin spreading beneath him. At the head of the ambush stands a broad-shouldered man with a notched cutlass, barking orders in a voice that claws at something old and ugly in your memory, a voice you have heard bellowed across a slave-pit floor.🔊………

log.action: Stride toward the sound of the whip.
log.narration: Turn 2 | Day 1, 6:04 pmStrength checkd20: 17 -- successYou close the last of the distance at a dead run, and the nearer raider turns just in time to see you coming, his eyes going wide over a scarred jaw. He wrenches his blade up in a clumsy guard, but you are already inside it, longsword screaming free of its sheath in one motion, and you put your whole shoulder behind the cut.Steel bites through leather and meat, and the raider staggers back with a wet grunt, blood sheeting down his forearm where he barely turned the worst of it.🔊………

log.action: Shout a challenge at the notched-cutlass leader.
log.narration: Turn 3 | Day 1, 6:05 pm"VALERIUS SENDS HIS DOGS FAR THESE DAYS!" you roar, the name torn out of you before you even know why, some old scar of memory answering the shape of that voice before your mind catches up.The broad-shouldered leader's head snaps toward you like a hound catching scent, and even across the churned dirt and screaming oxen you see his face change, surprise curdling fast into a wolfish grin. "Well, split my skull and salt the wound," he calls back, cutlass lowering an inch. "Korrag the Northman. Thought the pits had chewed you up and spat out your bones years gone." He does not charge. He watches you now the way a man watches an old debt walk back into his life, and behind him his raiders keep butchering merchants, unhurried, like men who know exactly how this ends.🔊………

log.action: Break off to protect the nearest merchant.
log.narration: Turn 4 | Day 1, 6:06 pmStrength checkd20: 13 -- successYou wheel from Theron's smirk and drive toward the merchant still crawling in the ash, dragging himself from beneath his overturned crate. The wounded raider lunges to bar your path, cutlass hacking low, but you catch the blow on your blade and shoulder him aside like a man shoving through a tavern door."Get behind the wagon, fool, unless you want to die out here!" you bark at the merchant, hauling him up by his collar with your free hand."Get behind the wagon, fool, unless you want to die out here!"The second raider peels off from the slaughter and comes at your flank, blade already rising, and Theron's laughter carries over the chaos like a man enjoying a show he has already decided the ending to."Let him play hero, boys! Makes the collar sweeter when we clap it back on!"🔊………

log.action: Finish the wounded raider before he recovers.
log.narration: Turn 5 | Day 1, 6:07 pmStrength checkd20: 16 -- successThe wounded raider is still catching his breath from the last blow, blood slicking his sword arm, when you turn the whole weight of your body into a downward cut. He gets his blade up too slow, too late, and steel finds the gap between his ribs and his collarbone with a sound like an axe through green wood.He drops without another sound, folding into the ash like a puppet with its strings cut, and the second raider slows his charge just a step, eyes flicking to his fallen companion."Gods below, he's fast for a chained dog!""Then don't dawdle, Renn, gut him!"🔊………

log.action: Cut down the flanking raider before he strikes.
log.narration: Turn 6 | Day 1, 6:08 pmStrength checkd20: 15 -- successThe one called Renn hesitates a half-heartbeat too long, spooked by his friend's corpse steaming in the cold air, and you close on him before he can set his feet. He swings wild, more fear than skill behind it, and you turn the blow wide with your crossguard and answer with a thrust that takes him full in the chest.Renn folds around the blade, mouth working with no sound left to make, and when you wrench your longsword free he crumples atop his companion in the ash. Only Theron remains standing amid the wreckage of the caravan, cutlass loose in his hand, and something almost fond curls at the edge of his smirk as he studies you across the corpses."Two of my best, gone in the time it takes to spit. Valerius always did say you were worth ten ordinary men in the pit, Korrag. Shame to waste that."🔊………

log.action: Taunt Theron while cutting down his last man.
log.narration: Turn 7 | Day 1, 6:09 pmBlood dries stiff on your knuckles, and you level your longsword at Theron across the two fallen raiders, breath coming hard and even."Ten ordinary men, and you sent two boys to do it. Valerius always was cheap with his coin, and cheaper still with lives that aren't his own."Theron's smirk does not waver, but something flickers behind his eyes, a calculation you remember from the pits, the look of a man deciding whether a beating is worth the trouble. He does not answer at once. Instead he backs a slow step toward the trees, cutlass still raised, clearly unwilling to close that distance alone now that his men lie cooling in the ash.🔊………

log.action: Use Power Strike to end this before he can flee.
log.narration: Turn 8 | Day 1, 6:10 pmStrength checkd20: 19 -- successYou do not wait for him to find his courage or his legs. You surge forward, boots tearing up ash, and put every ounce of fury behind the cut, screaming steel through the cold air.Theron gets his cutlass up just barely, but the force of the blow buckles his guard entirely, your blade shearing past it to open his forearm to the bone. He howls, stumbling back into a dead tree, cutlass clattering from fingers gone numb, and this time there is no smirk left on his face at all, only pain and something colder underneath it, calculation, the look of a beaten man already planning his next lie.🔊………

log.action: Charge Theron before he can flee into the trees.
log.narration: Turn 9 | Day 1, 6:10 pmStrength checkd20: 17 -- successTheron scrabbles backward against the roots of the dead tree, boots slipping in ash, his ruined arm clutched tight against his ribs. You close the gap in three long strides and slam your boot into his chest before he can find his feet, pinning him flat against the bark.He goes still beneath your weight, cutlass forgotten somewhere in the dirt, breath hissing through clenched teeth. There is nowhere left for him to run, and both of you know it."Easy now, Northman. Easy. You want answers more than you want my blood, I'd wager, or you'd have opened my throat already."🔊………

log.action: Kick away his fallen cutlass before he can grab it.
log.narration: Turn 10 | Day 1, 6:10 pmYou stamp down on the fallen cutlass and send it spinning off into the ash, well beyond his reach. Theron makes no move to chase after it. He only watches you with that same cold calculation, arm bleeding freely into the dirt, waiting to see what kind of man you have become since the pits.🔊………

log.action: Demand Theron explain what Valerius wants with me.
log.narration: Turn 11 | Day 1, 6:12 pmYou grind your boot harder against his sternum and lean down close enough to smell the fear sweat under the blood."Talk. What does Valerius want with me, and why send you chasing caravans to find it?"Theron laughs, a wet, broken sound, but there is no humor left in it, only the brittle defiance of a man with nothing left to bargain but words."You always were thick as a castle wall, Korrag. Valerius doesn't want you back in the pits to fight. He wants you back for the red rites, up in Ashenveil. Something about old blood remembering old chains. You've got a mark on you somewhere, don't you? Under the beard, along the ribs, someplace you don't look at in the mirror. He says it's still singing to him, all these years later. Says the Chained King wants his collar back."His eyes flick toward the wagon trail east, toward the wound in the world that leads into the Blighted Reach, and for the first time something like real terror crosses his face, worse than the pain in his ruined arm.🔊………

log.action: Press my boot harder and threaten his life.
log.narration: Turn 12 | Day 1, 6:14 pmCharisma checkd20: 16 -- successYou bear down until something in his chest creaks, and Theron's laughter dies into a strangled gasp. You drop your voice low, a growl meant for no ears but his."Old chains. Red rites. You're going to give me something I can use, Theron, or I open your throat here and let the crows have the rest of the story."Something in him breaks at that, the last of his nerve going out of him like air from a punctured bladder. He talks fast now, words tumbling over each other, desperate to buy the seconds they cost him."There's a fighting pit, new one, deep in Ashenveil, under the old tannery district! Valerius runs it through a front man, calls himself the Cage Master. Fighters go in ordinary and come out wrong, stronger than they've any right to be, eyes gone flat and hungry. He's marking them, Korrag, same as he marked you once, burning something into their skin that isn't just a brand. That's where he'll be. That's where you'd find him, if you're fool enough to go looking!"He slumps back against the tree, spent, his ruined arm shaking, and for a moment he looks less like a slaver and more like a man who has seen something he cannot unsee.🔊………

log.action: Bind Theron's wound to keep him alive for questioning.
log.narration: Turn 13 | Day 1, 6:19 pmWisdom checkd20: 13 -- successYou ease your boot off his chest and drop to a crouch, tearing a strip from a dead raider's cloak to bind the worst of the bleeding. Theron watches you work with something between suspicion and disbelief, too weak to fight you and too proud to thank you for it.You cinch the wrap tight above the wound, staunching the worst of the flow, and his breathing eases from ragged to merely labored. He will live long enough to be useful, which is all you care to grant him."Didn't peg you for a healer, Korrag. What happened to the man who used to finish what he started?"🔊………

log.action: Search Theron for anything marking him as Valerius's man.
log.narration: Turn 14 | Day 1, 6:24 pmYou kneel over his slumped body and pat down the blood-stiffened leather of his jerkin, ignoring his weak curse as you work. Beneath his shirt collar you find it, a small iron token stamped with a coiling, chained shape, threaded on a leather cord gone dark with sweat. It is the same design, you realize with a cold jolt, as the old scar you carry and never look at, the mark that has apparently been singing to Valerius across all these years."Careful with that. Wear it, and his dogs know you belong to him. Lose it, and they'll gut you for a stranger."You pocket the token anyway, whatever use it proves to have.🔊………

log.action: Rest and take stock of the situation.
log.narration: Turn 15 | Day 1, 6:39 pmYou rise from Theron's side and step back from the ruin of the ambush, letting the cold wind sting the blood drying on your knuckles. The crossroads lie quiet now, corpses and wreckage and one bound, beaten jackal all that remain of Valerius's reach into the wild. You have your answer, and it is worse than any lie Theron might have told you: the old man is not just a slaver anymore but something that speaks with the voice of chained gods.You crouch by the wagon, checking the merchant's cargo and your own aching ribs, and let the weight of the choice ahead of you settle in. Ashenveil waits to the south, its tannery district hiding a pit where men are unmade and remade into something hungrier. Theron watches you with the wary eyes of a man who knows his usefulness has an end date, and you have not yet decided what that end looks like.🔊………

log.action: Demand Theron reveal how to enter the tannery pit.
log.narration: Turn 16 | Day 1, 6:44 pmYou crouch back down before him, close enough that he cannot mistake the intent in your eyes."You've told me the shape of it. Now tell me how a man walks through the door."Theron shifts against the roots, weighing pain against pride, and pride loses as it always does with him."There's no door for the likes of you, not walking up and knocking. The Cage Master takes fighters through a butcher's stall on the eastern edge of the tannery quarter, one that sells more secrets than meat. You give the password, 'the collar remembers,' and they take you down through the cellar. But Korrag, listen to me. Once you're in, you're property again until he says otherwise. That's not a place you walk out of by strength alone."He sags back, the words costing him more than the wound did, and something like real fear finally shows plain on his face, not for himself, but for what waits below Ashenveil.🔊………

log.action: Rest and take stock of the situation.
log.narration: Turn 17 | Day 1, 7:04 pmYou settle back on your heels amid the wreckage and let the wind carry the stink of ash and old blood past you. Theron slumps against the dead tree, bound and beaten, no longer a threat, only a source to be drained or discarded. You check your own body next, the ache in your shoulder where a cutlass grazed you, the stiffness climbing your sword arm, nothing that will slow you long.You turn the iron token over in your palm, its chained sigil catching the gray light, and think of the brand you have never let anyone look at too closely. Whatever Valerius wants from you, he has wanted it for years, patient as rot. The road south leads to Ashenveil and a butcher's stall that is not what it claims to be. The road east leads into the Blighted Reach itself, where something ancient waits at the end of a chain that may not be as broken as you once believed.Theron watches you decide, and for a jackal who has lost everything, he looks almost hopeful that you might let him live to see how it ends.🔊………

log.action: Press Theron for the Cage Master's true name.
log.narration: Turn 18 | Day 1, 7:09 pmYou crouch low again, close enough that your shadow swallows him whole."The Cage Master. He wears a false face for the crowd, same as every coward Valerius sets between himself and a blade. Give me his true name."Theron's jaw works, and for the first time real hesitation crosses his face, not fear of you, but fear of a name itself."Careful what you go digging for, Korrag. Speak it too loud and things listen that shouldn't. His name's Kadrun Zethran. Used to be a moneylender before Valerius got his claws in him, now he plays showman for the pit and keeps the branded ones in line. But the name won't help you as much as you think. He's got wardens down there, things that don't blink right, and eyes on the surface too."He glances past you, toward the wagon trail and the wilderness beyond, as if expecting something to answer the name spoken aloud, and for a heartbeat you feel it too, some old scar along your ribs going cold.🔊………

log.action: Study the iron token for clues before moving on.
log.narration: Turn 19 | Day 1, 7:19 pmInvestigation checkd20: 14 -- successYou lift the token close to your eyes, tilting it so the ashen light catches the coiled chain stamped into its face. The metal is cold in a way that has nothing to do with the wind, colder than iron left in shade should be. Grooves worn smooth by countless thumbs mark it as old, older than Valerius surely, a symbol passed down through hands that feared it as much as they used it. You trace the links with a calloused finger and feel, faint as a held breath, an answering pull from the scar beneath your own shirt.The chain on the token does not close into a circle. It breaks at one link, deliberately unfinished, as though whatever it binds is meant to strain forever against a door left just barely open. You have seen that same broken link scarred into your own flesh, though you never let yourself study it so plainly before now.🔊………

log.action: Decide Theron's fate: kill him or let him go.
log.narration: Turn 20 | Day 1, 7:29 pmYou rise slow, the token vanishing back into your palm, and look down at the wreck of a man who once called himself your friend in the pits. Theron watches you with the stillness of a creature that has run out of tricks, waiting on the only verdict that matters now."Whatever you decide, Korrag, know I never wanted this life either. None of us did, down in the pits. Valerius makes dogs of us all, one way or another."You think of the two men already cooling in the ash behind you, of Renn's last breath rattling out around your blade, of every year Valerius stole from you both. Killing him would be simple, and something in your gut wants simple. But a dead man tells Valerius nothing, and Theron's fear of Kadrun's name still trembles fresh in his voice, more useful alive than silent.You crouch, cut the last binding loose from his good wrist, and haul him up by the collar until his boots find the ground."Run, Theron. Run far enough that I never have cause to remember your face again. If Valerius asks why you failed, tell him the truth. Tell him I'm coming."He staggers back a step, disbelief and gratitude warring plain across his ruined face, then turns and limps north into the wild without looking back, favoring the arm you broke.🔊………

log.action: Head east into the Blighted Reach instead.
log.narration: Turn 21 | Day 1, 8:14 pmYou turn from the crossroads and put your back to the south road, to Ashenveil and its butcher's stall and all the traps a city built by Valerius might hold. The wagon trail east waits like a wound in the earth, narrow and dark at the edges, cutting straight into the Blighted Reach. Ash thickens on the wind the moment you set foot upon it, and the smell of scorched things grows stronger with every stride, less like a forge now and more like something that died badly and never finished dying.The land changes fast past the crossroads. Trees here stand black and leafless, bark peeled back in curling scabs, and the ground crunches underfoot like old bone. Somewhere ahead, chained and patient, something has waited a very long time for a man bearing your mark to walk this road.🔊………

log.action: Search the wrecked wagon for supplies before leaving.
log.narration: Turn 22 | Day 1, 8:29 pmInvestigation checkd20: 11 -- successWait, you have already left the crossroads behind. But memory serves well enough. You crouch by the wreckage the ambush left in its wake, the wagon's frame cracked open like a ribcage, the oxen long fled or dead in the ash beyond.You dig through splintered crates and scattered sacking, ash sifting through your fingers with every handful. Most of the cargo is ruined, soaked black by spilled lamp oil, but you find a coil of good rope still dry beneath a fallen board, and a small clay jar sealed with wax that rattles faintly when shaken.The jar holds a handful of dried herbs, bitter smelling, the kind camp healers pack for fever and wound-rot. Worth keeping. You sling the rope over your shoulder and pocket the jar before the ash-wind picks up again, stinging your eyes and driving you back toward the eastern trail.🔊………

log.action: Listen closely to the unnatural quiet around me.
log.narration: Turn 23 | Day 1, 8:39 pmWisdom checkd20: 16 -- successYou go still, sword hand loose at your side, and let the world speak on its own terms. The ash-wind dies for a moment, as it does out here in fitful spells, and what's left behind is worse than any storm. No birds. No insects droning in the blackened brush. No small scurrying things fleeing your boots the way they should in any living wood.Beneath the silence, faint as a held breath, you catch it: a low sound like iron dragging over stone, arriving from everywhere and nowhere at once, then gone before you can point your ear toward it. The hair along your arms lifts despite the heat. Whatever waits at the end of this trail, it already knows the wind carries strangers, and something out there in the cinder-fog has just noticed you.🔊………

log.action: Push onward along the wagon trail into the fog.
log.narration: Turn 24 | Day 1, 8:44 pmPerception checkd20: 17 -- successYou set your jaw and walk into the cinder-fog, boots crunching over ground gone black and brittle. The trail narrows fast, hemmed in by the skeletal trees, their branches clawing low enough to snag your hair if you don't duck. Visibility drops to a spear's length in every direction, the world reduced to gray shapes and the taste of ash on your tongue.The dragging sound comes again, closer now, and this time it does not fade. Something massive shifts in the fog ahead, dislodging a spill of loose stone with a sound like a landslide given breath. You catch a glimpse through the haze, a shape too broad and too tall to be a man, moving with a slow deliberate patience that speaks of something that has never once needed to hurry.Chains rattle, faint and rhythmic, dragging somewhere beneath that hulking silhouette, and you understand in your gut this is no wandering beast. It is a warden, and it has been waiting on this road for a very long time.🔊………

log.action: Draw my longsword and press forward, alert.
log.narration: Turn 25 | Day 1, 8:44 pmWarden attack rolld20: 18 -- hitYou slide the longsword free, the rasp of steel loud enough to feel wrong in that dead silence. Ash falls off the blade like gray snow. You plant your boots wide, sword low, chainmail settling around your shoulders like an old promise.The fog peels back and the thing steps into view fully, a shape that was once a man and now stands twice as tall, flesh gone the color of scorched leather, hung with rusted chains that pierce its own hide and loop back into wounds that never close. Where its eyes should be there are only twin embers, dull and patient, fixed on you without blinking. It raises one massive fist wrapped round with a length of iron chain, dragging it off the ground with a shriek of metal, and starts forward.The Warden's mouth does not move, but a voice grinds out of the chains themselves, dry as a tomb sealing shut. "Blood remembers the collar."The Warden closes the distance in two lumbering strides, chain whistling as it swings for your skull.🔊………

log.action: Retreat a step to fight from the trail's edge.
log.narration: Turn 26 | Day 1, 8:45 pmDexterity checkd20: 14 -- successYou throw yourself back a half step, boots skidding through ash, the chain screaming past close enough to stir your hair. Your shoulder catches the twisted root of a dead tree at the trail's edge, and you plant there, giving yourself the narrow ground where the Warden's reach counts for less. The thing lumbers after you, iron dragging, its ember eyes never wavering.You've bought yourself a heartbeat. Use it.🔊………

log.action: Duck under the swinging chain and counterattack.
log.narration: Turn 27 | Day 1, 8:45 pmAttack roll (Power Strike declared)d20: 19 -- hitDamage rolld20: 6 + 1d6 Power Strike (4) -- 10 totalWarden attack rolld20: 11 -- missYou drop low as the chain hisses over your head, close enough to feel the wind of it against your scalp. Coming up out of the crouch, you drive your longsword in a rising arc into the Warden's ribs, putting your whole back and shoulder into the blow.Steel bites into that scorched hide with a sound like splitting timber, and dark ichor wells up black around the wound instead of blood. The thing does not cry out. It only turns those ember eyes down toward the gash you've opened, as if mildly curious that you could reach it at all.The Warden answers by wrenching its chain backward and lashing it forward again in a short brutal arc meant to crush your collarbone.The chain cracks into the dead tree beside you instead, shearing bark and splinters into the air. You're still standing, and now it's bleeding.🔊………

log.action: Lunge in with a Power Strike to its chained arm.
log.narration: Turn 28 | Day 1, 8:45 pmAttack roll (Power Strike declared)d20: 15 -- hitDamage rolld20: 7 + 1d6 Power Strike (5) -- 12 totalWarden attack rolld20: 13 -- missYou surge forward off your back foot, blade angled for the arm that hauls that murderous chain, putting everything you have behind the thrust.The point punches through scorched muscle where chain meets flesh, grinding against old iron buried under the skin, and the Warden's arm jerks with a sound like a rusted gate. Black ichor sheets down over the links wrapped into its wrist, and for the first time it staggers back half a step, chains rattling in a broken rhythm.It rights itself fast, faster than something that size has any right to, and its ember eyes flare brighter, twin coals fed a sudden gust. The dragging voice grinds out of the chains again, closer to a growl now than words."The King does not release what he has marked."It swings the ruined arm anyway, chain and all, aiming to crush you where you stand.The chain whips wide, gouging a furrow into the blackened earth instead of your skull. You've hurt it. It's still coming.🔊………

log.action: Drive a Power Strike into the same open wound.
log.narration: Turn 29 | Day 1, 8:45 pmAttack roll (Power Strike declared)d20: 20 -- critical hitDamage rolld20: 9 + 1d6 Power Strike (6), critical -- 24 totalYou plant your feet and drive the blade home a third time, straight back into the ruin you already carved along its arm, chasing the wound before it can knit shut around the iron buried in its flesh.The longsword sinks to the crossguard, grinding through meat gone half to char, and something gives way deep inside with a wet tearing crack. Ichor sprays black across your forearm, hissing faintly where it strikes exposed skin. The Warden's whole arm goes slack, chain slithering loose from fingers that no longer answer, and the ember light in its eyes gutters like a snuffed candle catching one last breath.The thing that was a man staggers, its ruined arm hanging dead at its side, chains dragging useless in the ash. It is not finished. But it is dying, and some flicker behind those dimming coals almost looks like it knows it.🔊………

log.action: Press the attack on its wounded chain-arm again.
log.narration: Turn 30 | Day 1, 8:45 pmAttack roll (Power Strike declared)d20: 17 -- hitDamage rolld20: 8 + 1d6 Power Strike (3) -- 11 totalYou bear down again, driving past its dead arm toward the ruin you've already made, sword seeking the last inch of resistance in that grinding mass of scar and iron.The blade opens a final gash across the wound-blackened links, and the Warden's whole frame shudders like a felled tower deciding which way to drop. The ember in its remaining eye guttered to almost nothing, it lets out one long groan of shifting chain and collapses forward, driving itself down onto your blade with its own dying weight.The Warden crashes into the ash, chains stilling at last, and the unnatural silence of the Reach seems to loosen its grip just slightly, as if the wood itself exhaled. Its ember eyes are dark now, hollow sockets in scorched flesh, and beneath the ruin of chain and skin you can make out the ghost of a brand scarred into what was once its chest, the same broken-link mark burned into your own.You crouch over the body a moment, catching your breath, and the shape of your purpose out here sharpens in your mind past mere curiosity about a dead trail. Valerius sent Theron's kind to hunt travelers on the crossroad. Something in this wasteland answers to the same brand burned into you. That means Valerius's reach runs from Ashenveil's tannery pits all the way out into this cursed wood, and whatever ritual he's building draws its power from something bound out here in the deep ash.🔊………

log.action: Search the Warden's corpse for clues or tokens.
log.narration: Turn 31 | Day 1, 8:45 pmInvestigation checkd20: 13 -- successYou crouch beside the ruined bulk of the thing, chains still hissing faint threads of steam where ichor cools against them. Wading through torn hide and iron, you search for whatever secret drove this creature to guard the trail so long.Wound deep in the chains wrapped round its chest, half fused into scarred flesh, you find a second token to match the one you took off Theron, this one blackened by fire and bent nearly double, but the broken chain design is unmistakable. Scratched crudely into the metal beneath the sigil, in a hand that was not the smith's, someone has scored three words: THEY WAIT BELOW. Whoever carved that warning did it before the Warden's mind was fully gone, a last flicker of the man buried under the curse.The ash-wind picks back up, dragging cinder-fog low across the trail, and somewhere ahead in that gray murk you sense the wood does not end so much as it deepens, drawing you down toward whatever "below" means out here.🔊………

log.action: Search the Warden's corpse for clues or tokens.
log.narration: Turn 32 | Day 1, 8:45 pmYou crouch beside the ruined bulk of the thing you slew, chains still hissing faint threads of steam where ichor cools against rusted iron. Wading through torn hide and buried links, you search for whatever secret drove this creature to guard the trail so long. Wound deep in the chains wrapped round its chest, half fused into scarred flesh, you find a second token to match the one you took off Theron, this one blackened by fire and bent nearly double, but the broken chain design is unmistakable.Scratched crudely into the metal beneath the sigil, in a hand that was not the smith's, someone has scored three words: THEY WAIT BELOW. Whoever carved that warning did it before the thing's mind was fully swallowed, some last flicker of the man buried under the curse fighting to leave a message behind.The ash-wind picks back up, dragging cinder-fog low across the trail, and somewhere ahead in that gray murk you sense the wood does not end so much as it deepens, drawing you down toward whatever "below" means out here.🔊………

log.action: Rest a moment and bind my wounds before advancing.
log.narration: Turn 33 | Day 1, 9:05 pmFirst Aid checkd20: 14 -- successThe ember in its socket flares once more, a final coal-glow guttering in the ruin of its face, and the chains grinding out of its throat shape one last broken word before falling still forever. "...free."You lower yourself against the twisted roots at the trail's edge, blood sheeting warm down your ribs where the chain caught you earlier. Working with quick, practiced hands you tear a strip from your undershirt and pack it hard against the wound, teeth gritted against the sting.The bleeding slows to a trickle, and some of the ragged edge goes out of your breathing. You dig into the herb jar salvaged from the wagon, crushing a pinch of the bitter leaves between your fingers before pressing them into the wound, the old camp trick doing its slow work against rot and fever alike.The ash-wind gusts low across the Warden's corpse, stirring the loose chains with a sound like something exhaling, and beyond the drifting cinder-fog the trail bends downward, the ground itself beginning to slope toward whatever waits below.🔊………

log.action: Study the Warden's chains for a way below.
log.narration: Turn 34 | Day 1, 9:05 pmInvestigation checkd20: 17 -- successYou haul yourself upright, ribs aching under fresh bandaging, and turn your attention to the great tangle of iron still fused into the Warden's corpse. The chains do not simply hang from the thing, they run through it, disappearing into old wounds and emerging again lower down, threading toward the earth like roots seeking water.
